title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Asha Mehta
description: Motivation: Improve OpenAI compatibility for function/tool calling by aligning tool_choice semantics with OpenAI's documented behavior, adding a robust mapping layer for tool schemas, and standardizing how tool messages are formatted across Redwood's API and SDKs. This change addresses customer integration issues (SUP-2108) where third-party models and SDKs expect OpenAI-style tool_choice responses and specific JSON schema mapping. Summary of changes: 1) openai-compat runtime: implement tool_choice selection semantics (explicit tool_choice + fallback ordering), expose chosen_tool metadata in streaming chunks, and ensure deterministic selection when multiple tools match. 2) schema-mapper: add a configurable mapping layer that takes tool definitions (name/description/json_schema) and emits an OpenAI-compatible parameters schema, including support for nested properties and required lists. 3) message-formatting: standardize tool invocation messages (role: tool, name: <tool>, content: JSON with pretty-printed vs compact mode based on client header) and add opt-in header for legacy clients. 4) SDK updates: typescript + python SDKs now surface tool_choice metadata on streaming responses and include helpers for validating responses against mapped schemas. 5) docs: add migration guide and examples for tool_choice and schema mappings. Checklist: - [x] Implement core runtime changes - [x] Add schema mapping module and tests - [x] Update TS/Python SDKs to surface metadata - [x] Add docs and migration guide - [x] E2E tests for streaming + tool invocation behavior - [x] Load test on perf-canary to ensure no latency regression Changes include small runtime refactors, tests, docs, and example prompts. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged unless a client opts into the OpenAI-compat mode via the compatibility header (X-Redwood-Compat: openai/v1). When enabled, clients will see tool_choice metadata and stricter schema mapping. See release notes for migration steps.
